newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SRI LANKA SAYS TO PUSH LEATHER EXPORTS.
newsitem.headline: SRI LANKA SAYS TO PUSH LEATHER EXPORTS.

text.p: Sri Lanka is to develop the leather goods sector to replace garments as its leading export, officials at the Industrial Development Board (IDB) told Reuters on Thursday.
"There is now a huge growing market for leather based products", Keerthi Senaratne, IDB's general manager said.
"It is easy to crash into this market," he said.
Senaratne said neighbouring India was aggressively targeting the lucrative leather industry, but there was still plenty of room for Sri Lanka to make an impact.
"There is also great potential for job creation as the leather industry requires manual operations," Vasantha Jayasinghe, chairman of IDB said.
Unlike in the garment industry, where most of the raw material is imported, Sri Lanka had enough local livestock to develop its leather sector, Senaratne said.
Sri Lanka's textile and garments exports in 1996 stood at 105 billion rupees, up from 95 billion in the previous year. Exports in the first five months of this year were 48 billion rupees.
Exports of leather items were however negligible.
Senaratne said IDB had spent 10 million rupees upto 1996 to develop 83 leather-based units. ($1-58.8 rupees)
